evidence.note: Claim: driver_conformance.py still builds hookio.Plan from the removed Hooks.normalizer attribute and hookio.NORMALIZERS/EMITTERS tables, crashing every command-hooked descriptor's conformance. Run before the fix: 'uv run pytest tests/test_driver_conformance.py -q' -> AttributeError: 'Hooks' object has no attribute 'normalizer', 20 failed. After building the plan from fieldmap(h.hooks.fields) and checking EMIT_VARIANTS: 59 passed, 82 skipped. CONFIRMED.
Read the brief rule/lesson/decision pack and r-gemini-key-load, r-task-phase-needs-wave; followed value generation rules (pin files regenerated, never hand-merged; selected-scope tests only).

Fixed ddflow/services/driver_conformance.py hook-plan construction; updated tests/test_driver_conformance.py to the field-map API; added adapters shell-line homes; reconciled adapters baselines (deferred_imports, unreferenced_functions, ports_without_fake).

chunk_findings.detail: The hooks failure path no longer detects an unresolved field map. `hookio.fieldmap(h.hooks.fields)` is passed straight into `Plan`, then `unresolved` only appends `"normalizer"` when `plan.normalizer` is not a `FieldMap`. If `fieldmap` returns a `FieldMap` for any mapping (including an unknown column or a non-mapping that it coerces), a command-hooked descriptor with a bad `[hooks.fields]` is reported `checks["hooks"]["status"] == "ok"`. If `fieldmap` raises instead, `run` aborts with that exception and never returns the failed hooks check the docstring promises. The old registry lookup failed closed for `"normalizer": "bogus"`; the renamed test only covers `emitter="bogus"`, so this input is now untested and wrong either way.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driver_conformance.py:49

chunk_findings.detail: The hooks check no longer fails closed on the descriptor half the module claims to resolve. The docstring says a command-hooked descriptor's field map and emit variant both resolve, but the new branch only tests `plan.emitter not in hookio.EMIT_VARIANTS`. The comment states that `hookio.fieldmap` defaults missing facts and drops unknown names, so it cannot fail. Given a command-hooked descriptor with `fields={"not_a_fact": "typo"}` and `emitter="plain"`, `checks["hooks"]["status"]` is `"ok"` and the run is treated as total. The rewritten test only plants `emitter="bogus"`; it never asserts a bad field map, so the property the old unresolved-normalizer test enforced is gone.
